newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Korean Air to expand asian cargo links.
newsitem.headline: Korean Air to expand asian cargo links.

text.p: Korean Air is planning three new Asian freighter services this year, South East Asia cargo sales and marketing general manager, Simon Yang told Reuters.

Yang said the world's third largest cargo carrier was forecasting four per cent growth in the Hong Kong air cargo market this year after KAL's cargo volumes from Kai Tak showed no growth during "a very difficult" 1996.

"It is very difficult to forecast the Hong Kong economy especially with the very big handover event but we are planning for a four per cent increase in Hong Kong volumes this year," Yang said in an interview from KAL's regional headquarters in Hong Kong.

KAL intends to increase its intra-Asian market share with the help of three new freighter services due to start this year having reported three per cent growth in cargo volume throughout the Asian region last year although this week it posted its first losses in its 34 year history,.

Shenzhen is to get a second weekly Airbus A300 freighter service on Thursdays to add to its Saturday service to the special economic zone in southern China from Seoul which began in November 1995. Yang said outbound load volumes had improved but inbound cargo was still "unsatisfactory."

The South Korean flag carrier also plans to inaugurate a freighter service from Seoul to Dhaka in Bangladesh probably via Bangkok and is also negotiating with the Vietnamese authorities to start a scheduled freighter service to Ho Chi Minh City, Yang added.

KAL has no immediate plans to increase its cargo uplift from Hong Kong, Yang said. It currently operates three freighter flights - two 747-400 and one A300 - from Hong Kong to Seoul weekly in addition to substantial belly cargo space available on 17 weekly passenger flights. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
